claim_summaries: A rational geometric grid converts the one-pass upper-estimate balancing step into exact rational ambient row scaling while retaining two-hole row maxima above 0.4075 and at most 1.

For explicit rational-complex F, a deterministic dyadic suppression epsilon=2^-Q gives a coordinate-dominated base within 1/128 TV of uniform complete-graph matching; Q=O(n^2+nL), with a rational uniform row scale placing all two-hole ratios in [1/4,1].

The activity interpolation and private-coordinate subdivision have polynomial binary descriptions, but the later empirical balance estimates and determinant-weighted mixing theorem remain unavailable.

Raw additive interval estimates alone cannot select a balanced scale when the maximum hole ratio may be exponentially small; this is an oracle-interface barrier, not a lower bound on algorithms given F.
next_gate: Acquire a polynomial-bit microscopic two-replica kernel with a polynomial Dirichlet bound so later balance intervals can be sampled and updated; continue auditing conditioning and exact subdivision costs.
